newsitem.title: GREECE: Foreigners escape from Greek prison.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners escape from Greek prison.

text.p: About 27 foreigners escaped from a prison in central Greece on Friday, taking advantage of lax security as hundreds of police guarded roads to prevent protesting farmers from blocking them, police said.

"The escape was planned. They knew that police were occupied with the farmers' protest and took advantage of it," a senior police officer told Reuters. "We have arrested 10 of them and we are looking for the others."
The convicts, mostly Albanians and Romanians, climbed the prison wall in the town of Larissa using bed sheets and then jumped to freedom. Guards opened fire but there were no injuries.

Scores of police officers have been stationed near toll booths on the main north-south highway outside Larissa for the past five days to prevent protesting farmers from blocking them with their tractors.
The farmers, pressing for cheaper fuel and state subsidies, blocked national highways for 25 days in December and have vowed to repeat their action unless the government yields to their demands.
